# MM-P1-L1-CN02 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge CNC turning center #2

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-CN02

Scope
This manual defines preventive maintenance tasks, safe work rationale, and acceptance criteria for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2, EQ-P1-L1-CN02. It applies to technicians assigned to P1, line P1-L1 and to engineering staff responsible for equipment reliability. This document supplements operating procedures and standard work, and references related documents SOP-P1-L1-03, SOP-P1-L1-04, and SOP-P1-L1-05 for operator-level steps and lockout/tagout requirements.

Background and purpose
EQ-P1-L1-CN02 is a production turning center used in hot forging finishing. Regular maintenance preserves spindle life, chuck integrity, and process accuracy. This manual provides the rationale for each task to prioritize actions that reduce risk of component failure, maintain concentricity, and ensure operator safety. Tasks are designed to be compatible with the referenced SOPs and to generate records suitable for trend analysis and root-cause investigation.

Tools
Approved tools and materials:
- Torque wrench calibrated and traceable to calibration records.
- Socket set compatible with chuck jaw bolt heads as specified by the manufacturer.
- Spindle warm-up control or programmable interface.
- Clean, lint-free rags and non-conductive brushes for debris removal.
- Inspection mirror and borescope for internal checks.
- Gasket materials and fasteners as specified by OEM manuals (refer to equipment file).
- Personal protective equipment per SOP-P1-L1-03 and SOP-P1-L1-04.

Procedure
Overview and timing rationale
Maintenance actions are sequenced to minimize thermal and mechanical stress. The spindle warm-up sequence reduces thermal gradients that can cause chatter or premature bearing wear. The chuck torque specification preserves clamping integrity without overstressing components.

Pre-maintenance preparation
- Review last maintenance entries for EQ-P1-L1-CN02 and the operator shift log to identify recurring issues.
- Follow lockout/tagout per SOP-P1-L1-05 before accessing guarded areas.
- Verify the torque wrench calibration sticker is current and record the calibration reference in the maintenance log.

Spindle warm-up
- Initiate the spindle warm-up routine using the machine control or the warm-up control panel. Warm-up is required to condition bearings and preload prior to load-bearing operations. The spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes. Allow the full warm-up time to elapse before proceeding to high-load operations or before performing precision measurement tasks.
- Rationale: Controlled warm-up reduces thermal distortion, stabilizes concentricity, and reduces the likelihood of differential expansion between spindle and chuck.

Chuck maintenance and bolt torque
- Access the chuck per OEM access guidance and SOP-P1-L1-04.
- Clean mating surfaces and inspect for burrs, scoring, or foreign material that would affect seating.
- Reassemble chuck components and install chuck jaw bolts. Tighten bolts in a crossing pattern to the specified value. The chuck jaw bolt torque for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 100 N·m. Use the calibrated torque wrench and follow the specified tightening sequence to ensure even clamping load.
- Rationale: Correct torque prevents bolt loosening under dynamic loads and avoids over-tension that can induce fatigue failure in bolts or distortion in chuck components.

Inspection and verification
- After torque application, perform a static runout check using an appropriate dial or electronic indicator setup to confirm chuck and spindle concentricity meet the machine capability as documented in the equipment file.
- Perform a controlled trial run at low load following the warm-up period to listen for abnormal noises and to observe vibration behavior. Refer to SOP-P1-L1-03 for acceptable acoustic and vibration check methods.
- Document any deviations and initiate corrective maintenance if runout or vibration exceed acceptable limits in EQ-P1-L1-CN02 equipment file.

Examples and common fault patterns
- Example: Bolt loosening observed after high-temperature cycle may present as incremental increase in runout readings across shifts. If this pattern appears, verify torque setting against the documented chuck jaw bolt torque for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 100 N·m and inspect for thread damage or galling.
- Example: Premature bearing noise following an incomplete warm-up cycle can be mitigated by enforcing the spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes prior to production start.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order with date, technician name, and start/finish times.
- Torque application log showing bolt identification and confirmation of the applied value: 100 N·m.
- Spindle warm-up log confirming that the spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes and indicating the timestamp when warm-up completed.
- Runout and vibration measurement records, annotated with pre- and post-maintenance results.
- Calibration certificate reference for the torque wrench used.
- Any nonconformance reports and corrective action records tied to the equipment serial file.

Acceptance criteria
- Chuck jaw bolts must be torqued to the documented value. Compliance evidence: torque application log entry showing bolts set to 100 N·m and signed by the performing technician.
- Spindle shall be warmed up for the full documented duration before precision operations or load testing. Compliance evidence: warm-up log entry confirming the spindle warm-up time for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is 21 minutes and timestamped completion.
- Post-maintenance dynamic check must show runout and vibration within limits specified in the EQ-P1-L1-CN02 equipment file. If limits are exceeded, the unit must be removed from service and a corrective maintenance work order raised.
- No visible debris, burrs, or compromised fasteners on chuck mating surfaces. Visual inspection must be recorded and signed.

References
- SOP-P1-L1-03
- SOP-P1-L1-04
- SOP-P1-L1-05

Revision control
All maintenance entries performed under this manual must be filed in the equipment maintenance record for EQ-P1-L1-CN02. Any deviations from this manual require engineering authorization and a revision to this document.
